days.findingJesus: From the first words, God speaks light into darkness. John says that Word is Jesus — present at creation, still bringing light when life feels dark. The serpent’s bruise in Genesis meets Romans’ promise: evil doesn’t get the last word; Christ crushes it.

Cain’s violence and a long line of names can feel heavy. Colossians lifts our eyes: Jesus is the true image of God and the One who holds all things together — including fractured families. Hebrews points to a better blood than Abel’s cry: Jesus’ mercy speaks peace.

The flood story is about judgement and a fresh start. Psalm 144 asks for blessing in ordinary life; Romans is honest that we all need rescue. The ark’s safety quietly sketches a bigger rescue — God making a way through the storm.

After the flood, God renews covenant mercy. Luke’s song celebrates God visiting and redeeming his people; Revelation’s mighty messenger reminds us heaven still acts in history. Rainbow promise leans toward a world remade in Christ.
Babel scatters proud plans. Psalm 2 shows nations raging while God installs his King; Luke notices God scattering the proud. Jesus gathers what pride divides — one people from every language.
Abram steps out on a promise. Matthew opens Jesus’ family tree with Abraham; Galatians says the blessing reaches the nations through Christ. Faith isn’t polish — it’s trust that God keeps his word.
Waiting, shortcuts and Hagar’s pain are real. Galatians and Hebrews say God’s promise doesn’t depend on our clever fixes — it rests on a better priest and a finished covenant in Jesus.
Covenant marks and a meal under the oaks show God coming near. Mark warns that clinging to wealth can block the kingdom; Hebrews names Jesus the mediator of a new covenant. God visits ordinary tents.
Sodom and fearful compromises are hard reading. The psalm remembers God noticing us in our low place; Peter says God knows how to rescue the struggling. Jesus is the safer refuge than any city gate.

Isaac’s birth and the mountain test stretch trust thin. Isaiah sings of the barren rejoicing; Hebrews honours Abraham’s faith. The ram in Isaac’s place whispers a greater Father who did not withhold his Son.
Funerals, wells and inheritance — life’s quiet chapters. Ecclesiastes is honest about dust; Romans wrestles with God’s surprising choices. The story still runs toward mercy we don’t earn.
Twins wrestle before they’re born. Hebrews anchors hope in God’s unchangeable promise. Even messy families sit inside a larger faithfulness — fulfilled in Jesus, the yes to every promise.
Deception and a ladder in the night. The psalm says God keeps watch; Matthew’s vineyard workers show grace that upends who “deserves” what. Heaven still opens over flawed people.

Love, rivalry and long years of labour. The psalm names loneliness; Song of Songs reminds us desire and delight belong in God’s world. Christ loves the church with a steadfast love no rivalry can cancel.
Leaving, fear, and a midnight wrestle. Angels encamp (Psalm 34); Ephesians says grace made Paul — and us — servants of a mystery now open: Gentiles welcome in Jesus.
Reconciliation and a tragic violation sit side by side. Hebrews remembers patriarchs who died still trusting. Jesus enters our violence-scarred world to heal what we cannot fix alone.
Altars, losses, and lists of names. The psalm loves a God who hears; Isaiah promises presence through deep waters. Jesus walks with us when the map of life feels only like genealogy and grief.
Joseph sold, Judah tangled — betrayal and shame. The psalm cries in the night; Matthew shows Jesus mocked by soldiers. God is not absent in pit or palace; the Suffering One understands.
Integrity under pressure. Psalm 1 roots the faithful person; Jesus calls us light. Holiness here isn’t perfection theatre — it’s quiet courage when nobody’s applauding.
Dreams, waiting, and sudden promotion. Wisdom comes from God (2 Cor 3:5). Joseph’s insight foreshadows a greater Interpreter who feeds the hungry world — Jesus, bread of life.
Famine drives brothers back together. Romans 8:28 isn’t a glib sticker; it’s hope that God works in grim chapters. Paul’s story (1 Tim) shows mercy rewriting a past.
Judah’s plea and Joseph’s reveal. Galatians ties blessing to Christ; Peter says prophets longed to see this grace. Tearful reunions preview the gospel’s reconciling heart.
Moving toward Egypt under promise. The psalm numbers our days; Isaiah says “fear not.” God goes with his people into strange land — as Jesus later goes with us into ours.
Settling, blessing sons, a lion from Judah. Isaiah’s compassion and Hebrews’ forever-priest meet in Jesus — the brother who saves and the King who never stops interceding.
Burial plans and “you meant evil; God meant good.” Acts proclaims Jesus’ death and rising; Romans leaves vengeance with God. Genesis ends pointing past the coffin to providence — and to Christ.
